questions.statement: Hans and Zacharias Janssen were the father-son duo who invented the first microscopes in the 1590s.
questions.explanation: The transcript states that Hans and Zacharias Janssen, a father-son pair of Dutch spectacle makers, put lenses in a tube in the 1590s and invented microscopes.

questions.statement: Anton van Leeuwenhoek’s microscopes could magnify up to 270 times, allowing him to see microorganisms as small as one-thousandth of a millimeter.
questions.explanation: The transcript notes that Van Leeuwenhoek’s microscopes had up to 270 times magnifying power and could identify things as small as 1,000th of a millimeter.

questions.statement: Joseph von Gerlock first succeeded in staining brain tissue by using an undiluted carmine dye made from crushed insects.
questions.explanation: The transcript explains that Gerlock initially had trouble staining brain tissue with undiluted carmine dye, and succeeded only after diluting it with ammonia and gelatin and leaving the sample soaking overnight.

questions.statement: Neurons have three main parts: the dendrites, the cell body (soma), and the axon, each with distinct functions.
questions.explanation: The transcript states that neurons consist of dendrites (which collect signals), the cell body or soma (which supports the neuron and contains nucleus and mitochondria), and the axon (which transmits messages).

questions.statement: Glial cells in nervous tissue function primarily to generate electrical impulses that neurons use to communicate.
questions.explanation: According to the transcript, glial cells do not generate electrical impulses but support neurons by providing insulation, protection, and tethering to blood vessels.
